summary: US-P3: Early-bird tiers switch over by the clock alone — no manual intervention
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** to schedule an early-bird price and its successors up
front, **so that** the price changes on time without anyone being awake for it.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-151 ✅ (closed — `price_rules`, the comparator and the
provenance shape exist; `SelectPricingRule` already takes the evaluation instant)

TKT-5's second COS: *scheduled price changes (early-bird tiers) apply without manual intervention*.
The lazy correct reading of "without manual intervention" is **no scheduler at all** — a rule
carries an effective window and resolution is evaluated against an instant, so the tier flips by
the passage of time and nothing has to run. A plan proposing a cron/job must argue why
evaluation-time windowing is insufficient.

> **ACs re-synced at claim** — one changed. "Caller-supplied evaluation instant" now means the
> **store/resolver** caller, not an HTTP parameter. See the `kind=claim` comment.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Migration **0013** adds `effective_from` / `effective_until` to `price_rules`, both nullable
  (unbounded), with `CHECK (effective_from IS NULL OR effective_until IS NULL OR effective_from <
  effective_until)` so a reversed window is unrepresentable (ADR-036 §4 step 2). The columns and
  the filter ship **together** — a column that accepts a timed rule the resolver ignores passes
  every all-NULL test.
- [ ] The interval is **half-open `[effective_from, effective_until)`** and that is stated in the
  OpenAPI description. An inclusive/exclusive ambiguity at a tier boundary is a real money bug.
- [ ] Resolution filters by the evaluation instant, so **no scheduled job, cron or write** is
  required for a tier to take effect. A test proves it: from one fixed dataset **with no write in
  between**, resolving at `effective_until - 1ns` yields the early-bird tier and at
  `effective_until` yields the next one.
- [ ] Overlapping windows at the same scope level resolve deterministically by a documented rule,
  proven by a test with two deliberately overlapping tiers. It must compose with TKT-151's existing
  tie-break (priority, then lowest id) rather than replace it.
- [ ] **§4 step 1 narrows**: the currency check now skips rules whose window has already closed
  (`effective_until <= at`) — they are inert. It still catches anything current **or still in the
  future**. TKT-151 checks every rule because with no windows every rule is unbounded; this ticket
  is where that becomes a real distinction, and the ADR already specifies it.
- [ ] Provenance reports rules that lost **on time** as `outside_window_past` /
  `outside_window_future` — the enum values TKT-151 declared and could not emit. An expired rule
  never appears as a winner; with all tiers expired, resolution falls back exactly as TKT-151
  specified.
- [ ] `effective_from` / `effective_until` in the provenance stop being always-null. **The shape
  does not change** — TKT-151 declared them required-and-nullable precisely so TKT-153's persisted
  snapshots span one format, not two.
- [ ] The window filter is **index-backed** per ADR-019 (result scoped *and* scan scoped, using the
  variadic `explainGenericPlan` and asserting the access condition, not just the plan's
  vocabulary); plain `CREATE INDEX` (ADR-020). OpenAPI regenerated and committed before the gate;
  the operation stays covered by catalog's own coverage test (ADR-030).
- [ ] The ADR-004 tier is **re-argued, not inherited**: a response whose correctness expires at a
  known instant cannot be cached past that instant. ADR-036 §6 already fixed `no-store` for
  sale-time resolution — state how that interacts with a tier boundary, and what a future
  browse-time read would owe.

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any
touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); public-read stories declare their ADR-004
TTL tier with rationale; entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002); money is integer minor units +
ISO-4217 code, floats banned (ADR-001).

objective.note: Early-bird pricing is table stakes; doing it by hand at midnight is the failure mode this removes.

scope.note: IN: effective windows on rules, evaluation-time filtering, overlap semantics, provenance of the active tier, TTL interaction. OUT: quantity-tiered / demand-based pricing, channel windows (TKT-17), commerce wiring (TKT-153).

uncertainties.note: Overlap tie-break (narrowest-window vs latest-start) is a design call resolvable in Planning against TKT-150's conflict semantics; it does not need a product decision.

approach.note: Extend TKT-151's rule table with the window columns and thread an evaluation instant through the same pure resolver — same test seam, table-driven with fixed instants (no wall-clock in tests).

first_slice.note: Windows on the existing rule shape; demoable by resolving the same data at two instants and getting two prices.

success.note: COS-2 of TKT-5, proven by the no-write-in-between boundary test.

context_memo.note: Baked below; governingAdrs resolved from docs/adr/ at 2026-07-30 and to be re-resolved at claim time.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.
Pin time-sensitive assertions to the DB's clock, not the test process's, so the boundary under test is the only moving part.

governingAdrs.why: THE SPECIFICATION, and it already answers most of this ticket: §4 step 2 (half-open windows + the reversed-window CHECK), §4 step 1 (currency skips rules whose window has CLOSED — the narrowing this ticket implements), §5 (outside_window_past/future, declared by TKT-151 and emitted here), §6 (no-store). Amended twice since this mémo was baked.
AMENDED by ADR-036: rule-based unit-price resolution is CATALOG's. The mémo's original entry said commerce owns it — do not follow it.

Two tests. And sharpened by TKT-151: asserting the index NAME appears is not enough — a read widened to scope_level alone uses the same index and scans the organizer's whole rule set. Assert the scoping columns are inside the Index Cond.
Re-argue the tier here rather than inherit it: this is the ticket that makes a response's correctness EXPIRE at a known instant, which is the actual reason for no-store.
Money stays integer minor units; a window changes which rule applies, never how an amount is computed.
Regenerate openapi_gen.go / api-types.gen.ts and COMMIT them before the gate — check-generate diffs against HEAD.
Migration 0013 runs out-of-band via the binary's migrate subcommand; the server path never migrates.
Plain CREATE INDEX for any window index.
Catalog covers its operations in its own coverage_test.go, not the smoke gate.

reference.summary: TKT-134's learning — pin the hold by DB time so release is the test's only moving boundary — is the closest precedent for testing a time boundary in this repo.
The existing operating-window columns on `performances` (migration 0004) show the repo's convention for representable time bounds.

Time-window fixtures must be relative to now — a calendar-literal fixture judged against now() is green at merge and fails once the clock crosses it; CI, mutation testing and review all pass because the defect only exists later. Build window fixtures from time.Now() with a deliberate offset, pinned once per run.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-152

**Gate 1 waived** (epic TKT-5's `kind=claim`): the agent performed `Backlog → Ready` as the owner's
proxy.

**Selection reason.** TKT-151 closed, so **both** TKT-152 and TKT-153 became claimable at once —
this is the first real choice in the epic. Taking **TKT-152 first**, deliberately:

- TKT-153 persists a **provenance snapshot** on the reservation. If TKT-152 lands after it, the
  window fields go from always-null to populated *underneath* stored snapshots, and TKT-153's
  format claim gets tested by production data rather than by a test.
- TKT-152 is additive to a seam TKT-151 already shaped (`SelectPricingRule` takes `at`; the
  provenance already declares the window fields). TKT-153 changes a **money path in commerce** —
  the riskier of the two, and better done against a finished pricing model than a half-finished one.
- Neither blocks the other, so this is ordering by risk, not by dependency. Recorded because the
  board cannot show a reason the graph does not contain.

**Not `risk:low`.** A migration, a change to the comparator's eligibility rules, and a currency-check
narrowing that ADR-036 spent two review passes getting right. The plan gate applies, resolved under
the Gate 2 waiver.

---

#### AC re-synced to TKT-151's decision

| Was | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "Resolution filters by the **caller-supplied** evaluation instant (defaulting to now)" | The instant is supplied by the **store/resolver** caller. It is **not** an HTTP parameter, and the boundary proof drives it at that seam. | TKT-151 established this and it is a security property, not a style choice: an HTTP-supplied instant on a sale-time price endpoint lets anyone request early-bird pricing after the window closed. The no-write-in-between proof works unchanged one layer down. Decided at TKT-151's plan-final (decision 4) and flagged there as changing a downstream ticket's ACs on my own authority — restated here so this ticket's plan draft sees it. |

Two ACs were also **sharpened** by things TKT-151's reviews established: the reversed-window CHECK
(ADR-036 §4 step 2), and the ADR-019 evidence now requiring the **access condition** to name the
scoping columns rather than the index merely appearing in the plan.

#### Context-mémo revalidated at pickup

Baked at decomposition (`capturedAt: 2026-07-30`). Since then **ADR-036 landed and was amended
twice** (TKT-150's own review rounds, then TKT-151's), and **ADR-002 was amended** by ADR-036 on the
pricing row. The mémo's `governingAdrs` are rewritten below to match what is now true, not what was
true when the epic was decomposed.

The learning already in this ticket's mémo — *time-window fixtures must be relative to now* — is
the single most relevant thing in it, and this is the ticket it was written for.

Branch: `TKT-152-effective-windows`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — TKT-152

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (config.models.plan), codex companion `task`, read-only, effort
`high`, at HEAD `7670f13`. Brief carried the ticket, the re-synced AC, the `governingAdrs` as
revalidated at claim, the two in-repo time-fixture learnings, and the code pointers.

---

The plan is evaluation-time windowing in catalog. No scheduler, cron, worker, or background write is needed: the same persisted rules resolve differently as `at` crosses a boundary.

I verified this against merged TKT-151 (`7670f13`), ADR-036, and the current board record. No files were modified; the two pre-existing untracked paths were left untouched.

## 1. Definition of Done

- Migration `0013` adds nullable `timestamptz` bounds and the named strict-order CHECK in the same change as resolver support.
- `PriceRule` and `PriceRuleInput` carry nullable `*time.Time` bounds; create/load/scan paths round-trip both.
- `SelectPricingRule` implements half-open `[effective_from, effective_until)` eligibility.
- Step 1 checks currency on every scoped rule except one already closed at `at`; a future wrong-currency rule still errors.
- Window-ineligible rules remain in provenance with `outside_window_past` or `outside_window_future`, including when all rules are ineligible.
- The existing hierarchy, forced partition, priority, and lowest-ID ordering remain intact.
- Overlapping eligible rules use explicit priority, then lowest UUID; window shape does not add an implicit precedence.
- `PricingResolverVersion` moves from `1` to `2`, because window eligibility changes comparator semantics even though the JSON shape is unchanged.
- A DB-backed test writes two tiers once, then resolves at `effective_until - 1ns` and `effective_until` with no intervening write.
- OpenAPI states the half-open interval; required-and-nullable provenance fields remain the same fields and now carry values.
- `Cache-Control: no-store` remains required and is re-argued against the now-real cutover boundary.
- Existing ADR-019 result-scope and scan-scope tests remain green against the updated production query.
- Generated Go and both generated TypeScript contracts are committed before `make check`.
- `make check` passes. No browser submission is required because this ticket changes no web write form.

## 2. Files

- [docs/adr/ADR-036-pricing-rules-representation.md](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/docs/adr/ADR-036-pricing-rules-representation.md) — document the overlap decision, resolver version, and present-tense cache argument.
- [services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0013_price_rule_effective_windows.sql](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0013_price_rule_effective_windows.sql) — new columns, CHECK, guarded down migration; no index.
- [services/catalog/internal/store/pricing.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/pricing.go) — model fields, step-1 narrowing, step-2 filtering, provenance, resolver version.
- [services/catalog/internal/store/pricing_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/pricing_test.go) — ADR-036’s TKT-152 truth-table rows and overlap cases.
- [services/catalog/internal/store/pricing_postgres.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/pricing_postgres.go) — insert, return, candidate projection, and scans for both bounds.
- [services/catalog/internal/store/pricing_smoke_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/pricing_smoke_test.go) — constraint test and no-write boundary proof.
- [services/catalog/internal/store/store.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/store/store.go) — update the store contract comments for windows and narrowed currency failure.
- [services/catalog/internal/api/pricing.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/pricing.go) — map effective bounds into existing provenance fields.
- [services/catalog/internal/api/pricing_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/pricing_test.go) — contract-validated populated-window response.
- [services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go) — fake store propagates window input into real comparator candidates.
- [services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml) — half-open semantics and updated provenance/cache descriptions.
- [services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go) — regenerated contract.
- [web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts) — regenerated contract.
- [web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts](/Users/matdupui/Sources/Mathieu/ticketing_system/web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts) — regenerated contract.

No changes are needed in `0012_price_rules.sql`, `season_smoke_test.go`, or `coverage_test.go`.

## 3. TDD order

1. Extend `TestSelectPricingRule` first. After adding only the compile-enabling model fields, these subtests are behaviorally red against `eligible := scoped`:

   - `closed_currency_mismatch_is_inert`
   - `future_currency_mismatch_fails_resolution`
   - `closed_rule_loses_as_outside_window_past`
   - `future_rule_loses_as_outside_window_future`
   - `effective_until_is_exclusive`
   - `effective_from_is_inclusive`
   - `all_tiers_expired_falls_back_to_base_price`
   - `overlapping_windows_use_priority`
   - `equal_priority_overlapping_windows_use_lowest_uuid`

   The red assertions are exact winners, resolved amounts, complete loser sets and reasons, and fallback state—not merely eligibility booleans.

2. Add `TestPriceRulesEffectiveWindowConstraint`. Before migration `0013`, it fails because the columns do not exist. It proves:

   - both `NULL`;
   - either one-sided bound;
   - `from < until`;
   - rejection of `from == until`;
   - rejection of `from > until`.

3. Add `TestResolveTicketTypePriceSwitchesAtEffectiveUntilWithoutWrite`. After the pure resolver is green but before PostgreSQL wiring, it remains red because the write/query path drops the bounds.

4. Add `TestResolveTicketTypePriceReturnsEffectiveWindowProvenance`. It is red until `server_test.go` propagates the input bounds and `priceRuleToAPI` maps them. It runs through `env.do`, so the existing catalog coverage and runtime OpenAPI validation gates see it.

5. Re-run the existing ADR-019 pair without duplicating them:

   - `TestResolveTicketTypePriceDoesNotLoadScopeIDCollision`
   - `TestResolveTicketTypePriceIsIndexScoped`

   The latter continues to EXPLAIN `priceRuleCandidatesQuery`, requiring `scope_level` and `scope_id` in the `Index Cond`, not merely the name `price_rules_scope`.

6. Regenerate contracts, commit generated artifacts, then run `make check`.

## 4. Migration

```sql
-- +goose Up
ALTER TABLE price_rules
    ADD COLUMN effective_from  timestamptz,
    ADD COLUMN effective_until timestamptz,
    ADD CONSTRAINT price_rules_effective_window_check CHECK (
        effective_from IS NULL
        OR effective_until IS NULL
        OR effective_from < effective_until
    );

-- No index: price_rules_scope remains the access path. See §8.

-- +goose Down
LOCK TABLE price_rules IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE;

-- +goose StatementBegin
DO $$
BEGIN
    IF EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM price_rules
        WHERE effective_from IS NOT NULL
           OR effective_until IS NOT NULL
    ) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION
            'cannot roll back 0013: price-rule effective-window data exists';
    END IF;
END
$$;
-- +goose StatementEnd

ALTER TABLE price_rules
    DROP CONSTRAINT price_rules_effective_window_check,
    DROP COLUMN effective_until,
    DROP COLUMN effective_from;
```

The down lock precedes the guard for the same reason as `0012`: without it, a writer could add timed data between the check and column drop. No `CONCURRENTLY` clause is introduced.

## 5. Comparator change

Add the existing contract’s nullable fields to both store shapes:

```go
type PriceRule struct {
    // existing fields...
    EffectiveFrom  *time.Time
    EffectiveUntil *time.Time
}

type PriceRuleInput struct {
    // existing fields...
    EffectiveFrom  *time.Time
    EffectiveUntil *time.Time
}
```

Step 1 becomes:

```go
func isPast(at time.Time, r PriceRule) bool {
    return r.EffectiveUntil != nil && !at.Before(*r.EffectiveUntil)
}

for _, r := range scoped {
    // at >= effective_until means permanently inert at this evaluation.
    if !isPast(at, r) && r.Currency != in.BasePrice.Currency {
        return RuleSelection{}, fmt.Errorf(
            "%w: rule %s is %s, ticket type is %s",
            ErrPriceRuleCurrencyMismatch,
            r.ID,
            r.Currency,
            in.BasePrice.Currency,
        )
    }
}
```

This deliberately does not skip a future rule: `effective_from > at` is irrelevant to step 1 if the rule still has any future.

Step 2 replaces `eligible := scoped`:

```go
eligible := make([]PriceRule, 0, len(scoped))
losers := make([]LosingPriceRule, 0, len(scoped))

for _, r := range scoped {
    switch {
    case r.EffectiveUntil != nil && !at.Before(*r.EffectiveUntil):
        losers = append(losers, LosingPriceRule{
            Rule: r, Reason: ReasonOutsideWindowPast,
        })

    case r.EffectiveFrom != nil && at.Before(*r.EffectiveFrom):
        losers = append(losers, LosingPriceRule{
            Rule: r, Reason: ReasonOutsideWindowFuture,
        })

    default:
        eligible = append(eligible, r)
    }
}
```

The strict CHECK means one persisted rule cannot be simultaneously past and future. Equality behaves correctly:

- `at == effective_from`: not future, therefore eligible.
- `at == effective_until`: past, therefore ineligible.

If `eligible` is empty, set `FallbackReason` but return `losers`; the current early return must not discard window provenance. If a winner exists, append the ordinary eligible losers to the window losers and sort the whole list by rule ID as today. `lossReason` remains responsible only for rules that survived time filtering.

`priceRuleWriteGateQuery`, `priceRuleCandidatesQuery`, and their `Scan` calls add the bounds in the same column order. The REPEATABLE READ transaction remains unchanged.

## 6. Overlap rule

Proposal: effective windows determine eligibility only. They do not imply precedence.

For two simultaneously eligible rules at the same scope:

1. higher `priority`;
2. if equal, lowest UUID.

This leaves `beats` unchanged and produces honest existing provenance: `lower_priority` or `stable_id_tiebreak`. It also composes unchanged with scope specificity and the forced-rule partition.

The domain reason is that temporal geometry does not reliably encode operator intent. “Latest start wins” makes a newly opened row silently supersede an older one, while “narrowest window wins” lets an unrelated end date decide the price and behaves awkwardly with an open-ended successor. In an append-mostly model, overlapping tiers should express intent through the field designed for conflict: `priority`. Equal priority is deterministic but intentionally semantically uninteresting.

The deliberate overlap tests should use real intersecting bounded windows, not two unbounded rows:

- differing priorities prove priority wins regardless of ID;
- equal priority proves lowest ID remains the final tie-break.

ADR-036 should record this choice. If the product instead wants “latest start wins,” that requires a new provenance reason such as `earlier_effective_from`; calling that loss `stable_id_tiebreak` would be false.

## 7. Boundary test

`TestResolveTicketTypePriceSwitchesAtEffectiveUntilWithoutWrite` should:

1. Seed the normal pricing chain.
2. Read one base instant from PostgreSQL:

   ```sql
   SELECT clock_timestamp()
   ```

3. Normalize it once with `UTC().Truncate(time.Microsecond)`.
4. Define `cutover := base.Add(time.Hour)`.
5. Insert once:

   - early bird: `[base - 1h, cutover)`, amount `3000`, priority `100`;
   - successor: `[cutover, NULL)`, amount `4000`, priority `0`.

6. Perform no subsequent writes.
7. Resolve at `cutover.Add(-time.Nanosecond)`:

   - early bird wins despite the successor existing;
   - successor is `outside_window_future`.

8. Resolve at `cutover`:

   - successor wins despite its lower priority;
   - early bird is `outside_window_past`.

Using a deliberately higher priority on the early-bird row proves that window eligibility precedes the existing comparator—it cannot accidentally continue winning at the boundary.

The bounds come from one DB-clock-derived base, not a calendar literal or repeated calls to either clock. PostgreSQL stores `timestamptz` at microsecond precision; truncating before persistence ensures the retrieved cutover is exactly the instant from which `-1ns` is computed.

The existing fixed `evalAt` in the pure test is safe to retain: it is compared only with other fixed values supplied to the pure function, never judged against `now()`. API tests that exercise `time.Now()` should pin one process-time base per test and use wide deliberate offsets, such as ±24 hours.

## 8. Index question

No window index should be added.

`priceRuleCandidatesQuery` must load all rules for the five derived `(scope_level, scope_id)` pairs because:

- an expired rule must be returned as `outside_window_past`;
- a future rule must be returned as `outside_window_future`;
- a future wrong-currency rule must fail now.

Pushing the time predicate into SQL would break all three requirements. The actual subset read remains organizer plus paired scopes, already served by:

```sql
CREATE INDEX price_rules_scope
    ON price_rules (organizer_id, scope_level, scope_id);
```

Adding `effective_from` or `effective_until` would not help a predicate that does not reference them. It would enlarge the index and tax rule creation/closure for no corresponding read benefit.

ADR-019’s two proofs already bind to this exact read:

- result scope: `TestResolveTicketTypePriceDoesNotLoadScopeIDCollision`;
- scan scope: `TestResolveTicketTypePriceIsIndexScoped`, including both paired columns inside `Index Cond`.

Updating the production query’s projection to include the bounds automatically keeps the plan test attached to the changed statement.

## 9. Risks and review focus

1. **Attack the overlap policy first.** Explicit priority is the least inferential rule, but equal-priority overlap still chooses an operationally arbitrary UUID. Confirm that the product does not want latest-start or narrower-window semantics before persisted snapshots make that choice expensive.

2. **Confirm the authoring scope.** There is currently no HTTP price-rule authoring operation; `CreatePriceRule` is an internal store seam used by tests. The board AC does not request a new authoring API, so this plan does not invent one. The story’s organizer-facing wording remains backend capability until a later authoring surface exists.

3. **Require the resolver-version bump.** The response shape stays stable, but version `1` cannot honestly describe both “windows ignored” and “windows filter eligibility.” This is easy to miss because TKT-153 has not started persisting snapshots yet.

4. **Review the no-eligible return carefully.** The current early return produces no candidates. A partial implementation can filter correctly while silently losing all expired/future provenance in the all-expired case.

5. **Check clock authority.** The stable DB-backed fixture uses the DB clock, but production’s evaluation instant remains `time.Now().UTC()` in `api.ResolveTicketTypePrice`. That is the merged security boundary and should not be replaced casually; it does mean process-clock discipline is operationally relevant.

6. **Check precision at the boundary.** The `-1ns` assertion is valid because comparison happens in Go after microsecond-precision bounds are read back. Building the comparison against a pre-round-trip timestamp could produce a false boundary test.

7. **Do not add a SQL time predicate for “performance.”** It would make the read cheaper only by deleting required diagnostics and future-currency validation. The scope index is the intended bound on candidate cardinality.

8. **Re-argue `no-store` in present tense.** Sale-time resolution is never cached because it feeds a money decision and can now become incorrect at an exact boundary. A future browse-only endpoint could cache, but its integer `max-age` would have to be rounded down and capped at the earliest relevant future `effective_from` or `effective_until`; that is a separate endpoint and contract.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Plan critique — TKT-152

**Critiqued by `main-agent`** (config.models.planReview). Cross-model invariant holds.

**This is the strongest of the three drafts in this epic, and the critique is short because of
that — not because it was skimmed.** Saying so plainly: a review that manufactures findings to look
thorough is worse than one that reports a clean pass. Three rejections would be dishonest here.

#### Existence check

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `eligible := scoped` is the explicit step-2 no-op to replace | ✅ `pricing.go:236` |
| the early return on empty `eligible` **discards candidates** | ✅ **`pricing.go:239-243` — sets `FallbackReason` and returns with `out.Candidates` nil** |
| `PricingResolverVersion int32 = 1` exists and is documented as a commitment | ✅ `pricing.go:85` |
| `ReasonOutsideWindowPast` / `Future` declared but unreachable | ✅ `pricing.go:74-75` |
| `price_rules_scope (organizer_id, scope_level, scope_id)`, no window columns | ✅ `0012_price_rules.sql` |
| the ADR-019 pair binds to `priceRuleCandidatesQuery` incl. the `Index Cond` check | ✅ `pricing_smoke_test.go` |
| latest migration is `0012` → `0013` next | ✅ |

**The early-return finding is the one that matters.** The draft caught it *before writing a line*,
from reading merged code — and it is exactly the AC ("with all tiers expired, resolution falls back
exactly as TKT-151 specified") that a partial implementation would satisfy while silently dropping
every `outside_window_*` loser. It is my bug, shipped in TKT-151, latent because no reason could
reach it yet. Being found by the planner rather than by the reviewer is the cheapest possible place
for it.

---

#### ✅ ACCEPT — the four decisions that matter

- **K1. Windows determine eligibility, not precedence.** The overlap rule is: filter by time, then
  the *existing* comparator (scope, forced partition, priority, id) decides — unchanged. This is
  right, and the draft's reasoning is the good kind: *"temporal geometry does not reliably encode
  operator intent."* "Latest start wins" lets a newly-authored row silently supersede; "narrowest
  window wins" lets an unrelated end date pick the price and behaves badly against an open-ended
  successor. Overlap should be expressed through the field built for conflict. **It also keeps
  provenance honest** — losers get `lower_priority` or `stable_id_tiebreak`, both true, instead of
  needing a new reason. And the draft names the cost: if the product wants latest-start, that needs
  a new reason value (`earlier_effective_from`), because calling it `stable_id_tiebreak` would be a
  lie. **Accepted.**
- **K2. `PricingResolverVersion` 1 → 2.** The JSON shape is unchanged, so this is easy to skip —
  but version 1 cannot honestly describe both "windows ignored" and "windows filter eligibility",
  and TKT-153 persists this number. Bumping now is free; bumping after snapshots exist is not.
  **Accepted.**
- **K3. No window index, argued rather than assumed.** The candidate query genuinely cannot filter
  by time, because all three of *report the expired rule*, *report the future rule*, and *fail on a
  future wrong-currency rule* require those rows loaded. An index on columns the predicate never
  references is write-path tax for nothing — which is ADR-019's own caveat, applied correctly
  *against* adding an index. **Accepted**, and the discipline is worth noting: the easy move was to
  add one and look thorough.
- **K4. The boundary fixture takes one instant from `clock_timestamp()`, truncates to microsecond,
  and derives both windows from it.** This obeys the relative-fixture learning
  (`2026-07-18-time-window-fixtures-must-be-relative.md`) *and* TKT-134's DB-clock rule, and the
  truncation is load-bearing: without it, `cutover - 1ns` compares against a value that did not
  survive the round trip. The draft also gives the early-bird rule a **higher priority** so window
  eligibility is proven to precede the comparator — the successor wins at the boundary *despite*
  losing on priority. That is the difference between testing the feature and testing that the
  feature is in the right place. **Accepted.**

Also accepted: the migration shape with the named strict-order CHECK and the lock-before-guard down
migration (mirroring `0012`'s corrected form); step 1's `isPast` narrowing, which deliberately does
**not** skip future rules; and the TDD order, whose first red tests are behavioural against
`eligible := scoped` rather than compile errors.

---

#### ⚠️ AMEND — 2, both small

**A1. Assert the resolver version as a literal, not against the constant.**
`api/pricing_test.go` currently asserts `out.ResolverVersion != store.PricingResolverVersion` —
which passes at *any* version, including one bumped by accident. With K2 deliberately changing it,
this is the moment that assertion earns its keep or stops meaning anything.
**Amendment:** assert the literal `2`, so a future bump is a deliberate test edit rather than a
silent one. Same reasoning as the golden-literal discipline the access lifecycle trail uses.

**A2. The all-ineligible path needs its own test, not just its own code.**
The draft correctly says the empty-`eligible` return must carry `losers`. But the AC it satisfies
("all tiers expired falls back exactly as TKT-151 specified") is *also* satisfied by code that
returns the right price and no provenance — which is the bug. **Amendment:**
`all_tiers_expired_falls_back_to_base_price` must assert **both** the base price **and** that every
expired rule appears as `outside_window_past`. State it in the test name or the assertion, so the
next reader cannot weaken it by accident.

---

#### 🔎 Pre-mortem

1. **The overlap rule is right and the product wanted something else.** The draft flags this as
   risk 1 and it is the correct first attack. *Mitigation:* windows-as-eligibility-only is the
   **most reversible** of the three candidate rules — adding precedence later is additive (a new
   reason value plus a comparator branch), whereas removing it would invalidate stored provenance.
2. **The boundary test passes for a clock reason rather than a logic reason.** *Mitigation:* the
   priority inversion in K4 — the successor must win at the boundary *against* priority, so a test
   that is accidentally comparing the wrong instants fails loudly rather than passing.
3. **Provenance quietly regresses in the one case nobody looks at.** The all-expired path. A1/A2
   above exist for exactly this.
4. **`no-store` gets re-stated instead of re-argued.** *Mitigation:* the draft's §9.8 already does
   the work — and its incidental point is worth keeping in the ADR: a future browse-time endpoint's
   `max-age` would have to be **rounded down and capped at the earliest relevant future boundary**,
   which is a genuinely non-obvious consequence of half-open windows.

#### Verdict

**AMEND** — zero rejections, two small amendments (A1 an assertion, A2 a test's strictness).
Everything substantive is accepted as drafted. The draft found a latent bug in merged code before
writing any of its own, argued *against* adding an index, and chose the most reversible of three
plausible overlap rules while naming what the other two would cost.

#### The mutation check, and what it actually showed

I ran F1's suggested mutation rather than trusting it. Result was **asymmetric**, and worth
recording:

- the **winner** path genuinely needs the sort and reddens without it — it concatenates window

- the **fallback** path does **not** redden, even with a reversed fixture, because `scoped` is

So the reviewer's proposed reversed-fixture test could not have failed. I kept it anyway and said
why in the test: it pins the **property** (id-ascending output), not the line that currently
provides it — which is what a consumer depends on.

#### Pass 2 — 4 findings on the fix diff. One real, three of my own sloppiness.

- **The documented guarantee was false.** My schema description promised the new test would catch
  any violation of the winner/fallback invariant. It would not have: the test covered a winner and
  an *empty-candidate* fallback, and mapping `fallback_reason` only when candidates are empty

- *"The schema cannot express it"* was **wrong** — OpenAPI 3.0 can, via `oneOf`. The honest claim
  is "not worth it here": a `oneOf` turns `PriceResolution` into a union in the generated Go and

- My fixture comment had `ruleB` and `ruleC`'s roles **backwards**. The fixture was right; the
  explanation was not — and a wrong explanation next to a right test is how the next person
  "corrects" the test.
- `assertLoserOrder` only compared against the caller's list, so passing a descending list would
  have passed while the failure message still said *"id-ascending"*. It now enforces ascending
